notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model entry for ros-wave-c-014 and reviewed_by stays null. No human review, ROS graph, camera, hardware attachment or hardware run is claimed. The pinned clone was only read; no upstream code was imported or executed and no network or pip install was used.

NO DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family 'ros' and helper 'RosDriver' match the pinned ROS 1 C++ node. This is a configuration-only RosDriver over rosbridge with no Python native class and no native.py; it never starts the upstream node. The package binds the standard cap.sensing.image.v1 through the RosDriver finite image selector with three fixed SD streams: /kinect2/sd/image_color_rect (sensor_msgs/Image, BGR8), /kinect2/sd/image_depth_rect (sensor_msgs/Image, 16UC1) and /kinect2/sd/image_ir (sensor_msgs/Image, 16UC1). Each capture returns a complete image artifact; the SDK emits a lossless PNG. /kinect2/sd/camera_info is a read-only CameraInfo observation for frame_id, width and height. Endpoint and type citations are the upstream README topic list (kinect2_bridge/README.md:85-92) and the advertise calls in kinect2_bridge/src/kinect2_bridge.cpp:513-518; all Facts cite the pinned clone at 0e2c5f63134a076606bb79963406e1d47f2da651. The topic list and C++ show the default base_name 'kinect2' and the composed SD topic macros; a deployment that changes base_name or namespaces the node must expose the resolved endpoints.

NOT COVERED: the HD and QHD streams, the SD image_depth and image_ir_rect variants, every compressed-image transport, the mono streams, the point-cloud topics and the depth_image_proc launch nodes, TF, camera controls, ROS parameter writes, full CameraInfo intrinsics/distortion/projection and calibration validity. Color, depth and IR are independent subscriptions, so this package makes no synchronized-triple or sample-age claim; the upstream README notes ExactTime synchronization is a caller choice. SD depth and IR are 16-bit samples: the 16-bit PNG preserves exact samples but depth units, calibration and a colormap are not inferred or published. The upstream min_depth and max_depth ROS parameters are not treated as universal measurement bounds.

FAKE: fake.py is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport, not a replay of captured ROS traffic. It answers the four declared subscriptions and models silent and malformed replies through options. Its 4x2 frames, header values, calibration and geometry are test data marked '# placeholder'; the real fixed SD capture size is 512x424 per kinect2_bridge/src/kinect2_bridge.cpp:138 and the README, and the smaller fake size is deliberate. The fake's byte arrays are placeholders, not device data. The deployed fake is event-driven F0 contract evidence with no ROS execution, wall-clock pacing or physical camera fidelity.

SAFETY: the device is a passive camera at R0. No Limit is declared because no action has a numeric input and the clone states no numeric bound for these fixed streams; site-limits.example.json is therefore not needed. The 2 MiB input, 2 Mi-pixel and 4 MiB message ceilings are client/transport conversion bounds, not camera limits. No stop, safe-state action or estop_physical_ref is claimed: the upstream callbackStatus starts and stops libfreenect2 streams as subscriber counts change, and closing a subscription is not camera power-off. The package is a passive R0 observation endpoint.

WARNINGS: the final gate reported only G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, expected because no actuating capability declares a limit and every other CL3 test passed. There are no G4.REF_VALUE, G4.REF_BINARY or UNVERIFIABLE_CITATION warnings. The gate ran with --backend fake; no hardware or allow-hardware path was used. test_driver.py retains check_driver(HERE, backend="fake") and adds eight repository-specific cases covering all three image streams, session-bound artifact retrieval, CameraInfo geometry, unknown/extra input refusal before image subscription, and malformed 16-bit/header replies with no artifact.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the three image streams and the CameraInfo reads against kinect2_bridge.cpp and kinect2_definitions.h at the pin (default base_name kinect2 composed with the /sd macros, Image and CameraInfo advertised at kinect2_bridge.cpp:513-518, BGR8 and 16UC1 encodings at 1380-1402, 512x424 SD geometry), all 18 facts, the image-artifact selector bounds and the R0 passive-camera safety statement; image capture is the primary interface and every encoding is one the SDK supports losslessly. The only defect was the fake's CameraInfo, which used the ROS 2 field names d, k, r and p in a ROS 1 message (the driver reads only header.frame_id, width and height, so no output changed). Reviewer changed fake.py (D, K, R and P as createCameraInfo writes them, kinect2_bridge.cpp:752-772) and the regenerated check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE and the digest unchanged. The 4x2 placeholder frames (512x424 real) are named in the notes. For the human reviewer: Subscribing starts the Kinect streams (callbackStatus, kinect2_bridge.cpp:785-810) and the last unsubscribe stops them; there is no stop or safe-state action because the camera has no actuation. Endpoints assume the default base_name kinect2 in the root namespace. Depth and IR are raw 16-bit samples with no unit or calibration claim.
